why: Ordinary palette placements had no native destination feedback before click, unlike copied building groups.
change: All native building palette kinds use the existing coalesced background native checker. Preview and commit share the starting-building constructor. Blocked sites have red footprint feedback and a written native reason; valid sites read Ready to place. Ordinary placements avoid serializing a full native snapshot just to report readiness. Commit remains independently validated.
coverage: All 22 current palette kinds: one eligible site and one occupied inland site each; actual successful placement, rejected click isolation, exact undo/redo, final Escape and reload. Hydro uses a native-eligible riverbank. Existing nine-building pipe/pump/cable preview, copy/move and exact history regression passes against these sources.
real_worker_failure: Browser routing aborts the real preview worker module. Unavailable feedback is visible, a valid ordinary placement still commits, and Undo restores the baseline. No page errors. Successful bounded cleanup in both browser runs.
visual_review: Individually inspected home-allowed.png, hydro-allowed.png and preview-unavailable.png. Native readiness and fallback messages are readable at full desktop size; overview zoom exposes the distant riverbank site. These captures establish UI feedback, not close-zoom sprite-art acceptance.
limits: Default completed-building recipe/appearance only; one allowed and one occupied site per kind. Does not exhaust boundaries, biome surfaces, every building appearance, battery/material/nature placement tools, worker failures during every operation, maximum connected groups, physical frame pacing or unfamiliar-player acceptance.
